core_obligations: Reduce to an evaluation statement (proof lines 14078-14084): because Hom(j_{U!}O_U, -) is the functor F |-> F(U), it suffices to prove H^p(U, M) = direct sum of H^p(U, M_i) for M = direct sum of M_i bounded below.

Handle sums of injectives (proof lines 14085-14093): for a family of injective O-modules I_i the hypothesis gives H^p(U, direct sum I_i) = direct sum H^p(U, I_i) = 0 for all p, so the direct sum of injectives is acyclic for the functor.

Conclude (proof lines 14094-14106): since M is bounded below there is a bound below which the cohomology of all M_i vanishes; resolving M by sums of injectives and using the acyclicity just established computes H^p(U, M) as the direct sum of the H^p(U, M_i), which is the required compactness statement.
proof_roadmap: Replace the Hom's by evaluations at U using the description of maps out of j_{U!}O_U.
Show that direct sums of injectives are acyclic for evaluation at U, using the hypothesis.
Resolve the bounded below object M and read off the commutation with direct sums.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for j_{U!}O_U to be compact in D^+(O): the cohomology functors on U must commute with direct sums (statement lines 14066-14075). The proof (proof lines 14077-14106) reduces the Hom-statement to evaluation at U, verifies that direct sums of injectives are acyclic for that functor under the hypothesis, and then computes the cohomology of a bounded below direct sum by resolving it. H2: one reduction followed by an acyclicity computation, written out.
